reuse.why: Builds on the existing WeekendRule type, getDateWithSkippedWeekend/getDayWithSkippedWeekend and d.isWeekend, adding a shared isSkippedWeekendOccurrence predicate that the template and upcoming-dates sites call.

duplication.why: The 'take extra occurrences, drop skipped weekend days, then move the rest' sequence is written separately in getNextDate (window 7) and getUpcomingDates (count * 7), and getNextDate re-inlines the predicate instead of calling isSkippedWeekendOccurrence.

placement.why: The rule predicate lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the weekend helpers and frequency is threaded through the RSchedule data in rule-utils, consistent with the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are limited to weekend handling sites, the recur data and tests.

maintainability.why: The daily rule is split: getDayWithSkippedWeekend now refuses to move daily dates while getDateWithSkippedWeekend still moves them, so each caller must remember to filter first, with ad hoc look-ahead windows per site.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getNextDate computes `!skipsWeekendOccurrences || !d.isWeekend(candidate)` itself instead of calling isSkippedWeekendOccurrence, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend is left unaware of the daily rule so callers work around it.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-then-move pipeline appears in getNextDate (find over a 7-occurrence window) and in server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates (filter/slice over count*7), the same logic reshaped differently.

one_place.where: The predicate is shared, but whether a daily weekend occurrence is skipped vs moved is decided per site: getDayWithSkippedWeekend encodes 'do not move', getDateWithSkippedWeekend still moves, and getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the template each apply the skip themselves.
